a1_answer:
NOVELTY STATEMENT — Standard practice delivers a MONITORING/INDICATION scheme (efficiency trip) based on effluent conductivity trends; your mechanism departs by inferring electrode capacity fade via the ratio of open-circuit voltage relaxation to charge balance derived from existing current and voltage logs, using the known faradaic capacitance relationship rather than direct efficiency measurement.  
PHYSICS CHECK — The governing physical relation is \( Q = C \cdot \Delta V \), where \( Q \) is charge passed, \( C \) is electrode capacity, and \( \Delta V \) is voltage change. For a fixed charge injection pulse (known from current integration over a standard duty cycle), a drop in \( \Delta V \) relaxation slope indicates a proportional drop in \( C \). Magnitude verification: For a CDI cell with \( C \approx 100 \, \text{F/L} \), a 10% capacity fade (\( \Delta C/C = 0.1 \)) results in a 10% deviation in the voltage relaxation curve relative to the baseline physics. This is detectable within 30 days of the 30-day pre-trip window if the fade rate is constant (\( \approx 0.33\%/ \text{day} \)).  
DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: driving variable = effective electrode capacitance \( C(t) \); the mechanism moves it **down** by accumulating irreversible faradaic charge and adsorption site blocking; this **reduces** the cell's adsorption capacity. The predictor does not move \( C \); it **detects the downward drift** of \( C(t) \) by comparing the voltage response to a fixed charge input. The "remedy" is not mechanical intervention but early detection of this drift.  

IMPLEMENTATION BILL —  
(a) Existing Cell Voltage Logger (ALREADY-RECORDED: "cell voltage... existing"); tag: (a)  
(b) Existing Current Monitor (ALREADY-RECORDED: "current... existing"); tag: (a)  
(c) Existing Effluent Conductivity Probe (ALREADY-RECORDED: "effluent conductivity"); tag: (a)  
(d) Edge Computing Module (runs algorithm on (a)-(c) data; no new sensors); tag: (a)  
(e) Algorithm: Compute \( \Delta V_{\text{relax}} \) per cycle from voltage logs during low-current periods; compare to \( C_{\text{ref}} \) derived from first-cycle physics (\( C_{\text{ref}} = Q_{\text{inject}} / \Delta V_{\text{fresh}} \)); tag: (b)  
(f) Threshold Logic: If \( C(t) < 0.9 C_{\text{ref}} \), trigger "Capacity Fade" alarm 30 days before estimated efficiency trip; tag: (b)  

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — Installability: None (uses existing logging). Operability: Automated (no operator action). Maintenance: Zero (firmware update only). Rough cost class: Same as standard practice (efficiency trip) plus minimal edge-computing hardware ($50–$100/cell). Operational loss: Zero throughput loss; detection occurs before trip. Parity maintained: The standard practice trips at 0% efficiency; this predictor warns at 10% fade, enabling scheduled maintenance instead of unplanned trip.  

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: 1. Extract 100 consecutive cycle data points from logs (voltage, current). 2. Compute \( C_{\text{meas}} = Q_{\text{inject}} / \Delta V_{\text{relax}} \) for each cycle. 3. Fit linear trend to \( C_{\text{meas}}(t) \). 4. Predict time-to-trip where \( C_{\text{meas}} \) reaches \( C_{\text{trip}} \) (from historical data). 5. Pass criterion: Prediction error < 3 days. 6. Falsification: If predicted trip date occurs >30 days before actual efficiency trip, or if FA rate >1/cell/year, reject. Duration: 100 cycles (≈30 days at 8h/cycle). Kill criterion: If \( \Delta V_{\text{relax}} \) is not statistically distinct from noise floor in first 10 cycles, mechanism is invalid.  

CONSTRAINT BIND — Primary stated indicator is **effluent conductivity** (efficiency trip). This predictor uses **cell voltage and current** as supplementary inputs to infer capacity, which is the root cause of conductivity-based efficiency drop. It does not replace the primary indicator; it provides early warning. The alarm is tied to the projected time to the conductivity-based efficiency trip.  

INPUT-AVAILABILITY CLAUSE — Required signals: Cell Voltage (existing), Current (existing), Effluent Conductivity (existing). All are permitted by the constraint "use only the existing cell voltage, current and effluent conductivity." No new instrumentation.  

COST-PRICING CLAUSE — No setpoint or duty-cycle modulation is proposed; therefore, no operational cost line is required. The predictor runs in the background with negligible energy consumption (<1W).  

MECHANISM CLASS: Electrode Capacity Drift Inference via Voltage Relaxation Analysis
